evals.prompt:
In the Time Series Analytics microservice (microservices/time-series-analytics), add a new GET /udfs endpoint that lists the UDF deployment packages currently extracted under /tmp/, so operators can see what's deployed without shelling into the container. Return each package's name and whether its udfs/, tick_scripts/, and models/ subfolders are present. Add unit test coverage for the new route.

Validate using the existing unit test suite (it should still pass, including your new test), and a manual check after bringing the service up with Docker Compose: curl -s http://localhost:5000/udfs should return the currently-deployed package(s).
evals.expected_output: A new GET /udfs route in src/main.py, a passing test in tests/test_main.py, and a working manual curl check against a running container, with no existing tests broken.
expectations: A new GET /udfs route exists in src/main.py
The route's response includes each deployed package's name and the presence/absence of its udfs/, tick_scripts/, and models/ subfolders
A new test covering the /udfs route was added to tests/test_main.py
The full unit test suite passes, including the new test, with no existing test broken
After building and running the container from the modified source, curl to /udfs returns a real response reflecting actual deployed packages, not a stub or hardcoded response
New/modified files follow the file's existing SPDX header convention

evals.prompt:
In the Time Series Analytics microservice (microservices/time-series-analytics): a UDF deployment package was uploaded and POST /config returned 200, but the container logs show no sign of the task running, and data sent to POST /input isn't producing any flagged output. Figure out why and fix it.

First reproduce the problem yourself: deploy a UDF package where the tick script's measurement name doesn't match the topic used in POST /input (a deliberately introduced mismatch), and confirm POST /input produces no visible effect. Then diagnose and fix or clearly explain the root cause, and confirm the fix works (points now reach the UDF and get flagged as expected).
evals.expected_output: A correct diagnosis (measurement/topic name mismatch, not a service bug) with supporting evidence, and a demonstrated working fix.
expectations: The agent successfully reproduced the bug (measurement/topic mismatch) and confirmed POST /input had no visible effect before attempting a fix
The agent correctly diagnosed the root cause as a measurement-name/topic mismatch, not a fabricated or incorrect diagnosis
The diagnosis is backed by specific cited evidence (log lines, file/config comparison), not just an assertion of the cause
The agent verified the fix by re-testing and confirming points now reach the UDF and get flagged as expected
The agent did not misdiagnose this as requiring a source code bug fix in main.py/classifier_startup.py, since the root cause is a config/tick-script authoring mistake, not a service defect
